research_question: Can the current REM-AlignNet-MTL and adapted radarODE-MTL checkpoints be evaluated under a record-level long ECG assembly protocol using identical MMECG LOSO test windows?
hypothesis: A metadata-preserving record-level assembly evaluator can expose the difference between REM-AlignNet-MTL continuous-window reconstruction and radarODE-MTL ECG_shape morphology reconstruction, while clearly marking oracle-cycle assembly as pilot evidence.
protocol: Fold-01 strict LOSO record-level overlap-add assembly on processed H5 windows. REM uses full-window OLA; radarODE uses ECG_shape placed into GT center-cycle bounds as an oracle diagnostic.
baseline: Adapted radarODE-MTL/EGA strict LOSO checkpoint under radarode_shape_oracle_cycle_ola
changed_variable: Assembly/evaluation protocol, not model architecture or training.
controlled_variables: Same fold_01 MMECG strict LOSO test.h5
success_criteria: Script produces record_metrics_long.csv, window_metrics_long.csv, predictions_long.npz, and global_summary_long.json for both methods.
Summary explicitly labels oracle-cycle assembly as non-final pilot evidence.
Record-level metrics can be inspected without using Shape-200 averages as final long ECG claims.
checkpoint_selection: Use existing saved best checkpoints from the pilot runs without changing selection.
estimated_compute: Inference only, fold_01, under 30 minutes on one GPU.
failure_interpretation: If assembly fails or produces very low coverage, current artifacts/protocol are insufficient and the next step is predicted-anchor export plus long-assembly protocol revision.
notes: This pilot validates the evaluator and evidence format. It is not a final Q1 table.
